content:
maria: Ran a quantized sweep (int4/ql3 variants) on llamaX-13B for long-context priming today. Repro steps below and one clear failure when rope_scale != 1.0 and using kv_prefill + interleaved prefix.

josh: ack — can you paste the exact command and the minimal failing prompt?

maria: Command:```bash
python tests/longctx_repro.py \\\--model artifacts/llamaX_q4 \\\--rope-scale 1.02 \\\--prompt-file tests/long_prompts/chatty_long.txt \\\--max-tokens 12000 \\\--kv-mode prefill \\\--prefill-stride 512
```
Prompt is a ~11k token conversational thread with repeated named entities and a short system prefix inserted at several points.

josh: What was the symptom? Divergence from float baseline or outright corruption?

maria: Divergence. At token ~9461 tokens we start getting shifted tokens. Baseline float32 generates: 
"...and the meeting in San Jose ended in applause."
Quantized+rope_scale=1.02 generates: 
"...and the meeting in San Jose ended in applause." (extra 'l') then later token alignment drifts.

arjun: small spelling differences usually point to numeric noise, but drift that amplifies after a wrap is suspicious. Is this only when prefill is used?

maria: I ran three variants: prefill, continuous-batching (kv streaming), and no-prefill. Failure reproduces on prefill and intermittent on streaming; does NOT reproduce on no-prefill. So points at prefill buffer/indexing interaction.

sophia: Can you paste kv-index dump around the boundary where it flips?

maria: snippet:```
KV-DUMP idx_range [9216..9728]
shard0 keys: [9216..9471]
shard1 keys: [9472..9727]
last_prefill_stride: 512
observed-prefill-offset: 9472
rotary-scale: 1.02
checksum(shard0 head)=0x4f9a
checksum(shard1 head)=0x4f9b
Mismatch detected at pos 9473 -> kv_lookup returned token_id 1243 but baseline 1271
```

arjun: checksums close but not identical. That could be due to quantized kernel selection (int4 path) picking slightly different rot-phase application. Could you try forcing the float kernel path but keep quant weights (i.e., run quant weights on float execution) to separate weight quant noise vs runtime rotor math?

maria: Try run queued:```bash
python tests/longctx_repro.py \\\--model artifacts/llamaX_q4 \\\--rope-scale 1.02 \\\--use-float-kernel True \\\--kv-mode prefill
```
I'll report back.

(dev-bot): CI job longctx/2798 started on runner gpu-x1.

maria: Quick results: forcing float kernel removed the drift (alignment remains consistent), so kernel math + quant path looks implicated.

josh: Nice isolate. Next step: which kernel op? RoPE application happens in attention precompute or q/k scaling spot. If we log rotary multiplication outputs pre-quant and post-quant kernel we can compare.

sophia: Also try adjusting rope_scale to slightly <1 (0.995) to see if drift direction flips — that can help validate a sign/sampling bias in the interpolation.

maria: Did that: rope_scale=0.995 produced the opposite subtle shift earlier (~9032 tokens) but same amplification pattern.

arjun: Hypothesis: int4 kernel loads packed activations and uses approximate sin/cos interpolation table indexed by scaled positions. When prefill writes kv shards with stride 512, boundary alignment causes index rounding that the packed-loader mishandles for non-integer scaled positions.

josh: Can we repro on a smaller synthetic to iterate faster? A synthetic prompt with two repeated sections to force prefix overlap and a short window wrap.

maria: I created a minimal repro: 3 repeats of a 4k token paragraph + interleaved 4-token system prompt. Repro command:```bash
python tests/longctx_repro.py \\\--model artifacts/llamaX_q4 \\\--rope-scale 1.02 \\\--prompt-file tests/long_prompts/synth_overlap.txt \\\--max-tokens 14000 \\\--prefill-stride 4096
```
This reproduces in ~30s on a V100.

sophia: Good. Please attach the failing token diff and a minimal reproducer for infra to run. I'll open a bench ticket.

maria: Attached repro (pushed to s3: s3://redwood-ml-repros/2798765432/synth_overlap.tar.gz) — includes seeds, config, and kv dumps.

josh: For remediation: we can attempt 1) fix the packed-loader edge case, 2) force float-kernel at boundaries, or 3) tighten prefill stride alignment (make stride a divisor of shard-block-size). Which is least risky for a patch?

arjun: 3 is a config mitigation; easy and low-risk. 2 is a runtime toggle - ok short term. 1 is permanent fix but needs kernel change + perf test.

sophia: Create a canary on dedicated with forced float-kernel for customers who hit this and add a telemetry flag to detect kv-index checksum drift > threshold.

maria: I'll open the bug with triage notes + perf numbers. Quick perf note: int4 path was ~2.4x faster; forcing float-kernel slows us to ~1.6x, so we lose some benefit but acceptable as a temporary rollback on long-context heavy customers.

(dev-bot): CI run longctx/2798 finished — 1 failing test (longctx_kv_prefill_collision). Logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/2798

josh: Thanks, will follow up with a kernel PR draft tomorrow. :thumbsup:
